headline: Farid Teymouri Launches Personal Developer Portfolio Website
summary: A software and web developer launches a personal portfolio to document their journey and showcase projects, built with Laravel & Nuxt.js.
details: Farid Teymouri, a software and web developer with expertise in penetration testing and server/site security, has launched their personal portfolio website. The developer began their professional career in 2009, focusing on software development, DevOps, and web security.

The portfolio website is built using Laravel and Nuxt.js, showcasing Teymouri's skills and projects. It serves as a platform to document their continuous journey in building software and sharing insights.

Teymouri has extensive experience, including work as a Software Developer at Maral Host Web Hosting from 2020 to 2022, where they completed projects involving CMS development and WHMCS modules, earning an official employer satisfaction certificate.

The website also highlights Teymouri's other contributions and profiles, including links to their GitHub, dev.to blog, and Social X presence, providing a comprehensive view of their professional background and work.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI CEO Sam Altman]] says IPO is 'ill-advised' for 2026
headline: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says IPO is 'ill-advised' for 2026
summary: Altman states that going public now would be a bad moment, with the company aiming for readiness when the business and societal context are right.
details: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has indicated that the company will not be going public in 2026, calling it an 'ill-advised moment' for such a move.
Altman explained that OpenAI will go public "when we're ready, which is when the business is ready, when we feel ready from what the moment is like in society with this technology."

This statement comes despite reports that OpenAI has hired bankers and lawyers with the goal of an IPO in late 2026, with some sources suggesting a shift towards 2027 due to market volatility and internal financial considerations.
The CEO emphasized that the company has 'a lot of stuff to do' before considering a public offering, prioritizing readiness over a specific timeline.
